newsitem.title: GERMANY: German GDP growth stagnated in final quarter 96.
newsitem.headline: German GDP growth stagnated in final quarter 96.

text.p: German gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 1.4 percent in 1996 but growth stagnated in the final quarter compared to the previous quarter, the Federal Statistics Office said on Wednesday.
The 1996 figure confirms preliminary data released in January and represents a slowdown from 1995 growth of 1.9 percent.
But figures for the third quarter were revised down, with year-on-year growth cut to 2.3 percent from 2.4, and growth against the previous quarter cut by a half point to 0.5 percent.
Economists polled by Reuters had expected the 1996 growth rate to be revised down to 1.3 percent and had predicted a slight decline in fourth-quarter GDP by 0.1 or 0.2 percent from the third quarter.

The Economics Ministry's quarter-on-quarter figures were rounded to the nearest half percentage point. It said that the main growth impulses came from the services sector, which grew by 4.5 percent in the fourth quarter from a year earlier.
The data come a day ahead of unemployment figures for February which economists expect to show another post-war record of 4.32 million on a seasonally-adjusted basis, up about 20,000 from January.

The ministry said that despite growth in the economy, the size of the German workforce declined by 491,000 in the fourth quarter compared to a year earlier, while the number of registered unemployed rose on average by 348,000.

Slow growth and rising unemployment with the resulting rise in benefit payouts and loss of tax revenues has sparked fears that Germany may not be able to qualify for the planned European single currency in what could endanger the entire project, scheduled to begin on January 1, 1999.

But economists see almost no chance of the Bundesbank cutting interest rates soon since price rises have accelerated in recent months. The central bank holds its next policymaking council meeting on Thursday.
